# Conformance — every spec vector, and what proves it

**Generated by `scripts/check-vectors.py`. Do not hand-edit.**

One row per vector in [proxy-behavior](../specs/proxy-behavior.md) §12, [e2e-probe](../specs/e2e-probe.md) §10, [registrar-auth](../specs/registrar-auth.md) §8, [hook-framework](../specs/hook-framework.md) §9, [location-service](../specs/location-service.md) §9, [media-relay](../specs/media-relay.md) §12, [number-normalisation](../specs/number-normalisation.md) §11, [affinity-token](../specs/affinity-token.md) §10, [affinity-token](../specs/affinity-token.md) §10, [cluster-config](../specs/cluster-config.md) §12, [asserted-identity](../specs/asserted-identity.md) §13, [hook-framework](../specs/hook-framework.md) §9.1, [sipx-cluster-crd](../specs/sipx-cluster-crd.md) §10, [session-service](../specs/session-service.md) §6 and [operational-capability-baseline](../specs/operational-capability-baseline.md) §5.

A row is *proved* when a test in the workspace covers it **and** compares every value the
row states, *shape only* when a test covers it but never compares a value it states, and
*deferred* when [vector-scope.toml](vector-scope.toml) says why and names the story that
will.

**128 of 576 rows proved**; 19 covered for shape only; 429 deferred.

Σ over the 61 sections below is 576, so every row counted above is shown in exactly one table.

## What these words mean

**Proved** means: a test named for the row exists and runs, and — where the row's `Expect`
column states a number — some assertion in that test compares that number. `CF-12` added
the second half. Before it, `PB-F-1` read *Timer C set 180 s* and its test asserted only
`[Kind::ResolveTargets, Kind::Forward, Kind::SetTimer]`, so the row and the code never met;
the row was wrong about the value for the project's whole life and the report said proved
throughout.

**Shape only** means the row states a value and nothing in its proof compares it. The test
runs and the behaviour it does check is checked; the quantity the row exists to pin is not.
These rows are named in [vector-scope.toml](vector-scope.toml) with what the test asserts
instead, and they do not count towards *proved*.

**What proved still does not mean.** That the assertion compares the *right* thing: any
assertion in the test satisfies the check, so a value used as stimulus and re-asserted
elsewhere counts. That the test agrees with the row — `PB-R-5` states `486` and its test
asserts `404`; the check can see a number missing, not which of the two is wrong. That a
row stating no number is checked at all beyond its name: for those, *proved* is worth
exactly what the test is worth. And nothing here says the spec itself is right.

## Registrar auth — replay and retransmission (§3, §6, §7)

| Row | Status | Proved by / deferred to |
|---|---|---|
| `RA-R-1` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs`, `crates/sipx-clstr-sim/tests/register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-2` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs`, `crates/sipx-clstr-sim/tests/register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-3` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-4` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-5` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-6` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-registrar/tests/vectors_register_auth.rs`, `crates/sipx-clstr-sim/tests/register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-7` | proved | `crates/sipx-clstr-sim/tests/register_auth.rs` |
| `RA-R-8` | deferred | `CX-5` — `N1`, nonce uniqueness per challenge — registrar-auth §6.1. Deferred because it cannot be covered from this repository *and* because it does not hold: nonce minting is `sipx-ua::challenge`'s (an auth primitive, AGENTS.md #6), and at the pinned `v0.10.0` its mint is `<issued-at in hex>.<HMAC over issued-at and realm>` — a pure function of the second, the realm and the secret. Two users of one tenant challenged in the same second hold one nonce and therefore one replay counter, and the second correct credential is refused as `RA-R-2` with a `401` carrying no `stale`. The row states the requirement rather than the current behaviour, so it fails today by construction; that is the point of writing it. Filed as an `open` row in docs/upstream.md with the reproduction. Coverage is CX-5's remaining acceptance — a kernel that mints per-challenge entropy, a pinned release carrying it, and the harness scenario that challenges two users within one simulated second and requires both to authenticate. CX-5 therefore stays open: closing it would leave this deferral naming a story nobody will act on. |

## SipxCluster — admission, cluster-scope (§10)

| Row | Status | Proved by / deferred to |
|---|---|---|
| `SC-A-1` | deferred | `KO-3` — A1/A2: an unrecognised key under `spec.registrar` is refused with the error `cluster-config` §8 already produces, in `path` order, and nothing is created. The loader that produces that error exists (`DP-8`); what does not is the webhook that runs it before admission and turns its result into a rejection. Testable when a verdict has a producer. |
| `SC-A-2` | deferred | `KO-3` — A4: two zones, `edge` placed in only one, rejected naming the other. This is the row that proves the cluster-scope half of §8 — no single node's projection can see it, because a node projects its own zone and a zone with no edge is a fact about the set. It needs the admission path specifically, not a loader test. |
| `SC-A-3` | deferred | `KO-3` — A5: a declared role with no listener naming it is refused at admission, naming the role — rather than becoming a pod that fails `cluster-config` `P4` after being created. The row's whole content is *when* the failure happens, so it cannot be proved anywhere but the webhook. |
| `SC-A-4` | deferred | `KO-3` — A6: a `managed` media pool without a `portRange` is refused, naming the pool. Needs the webhook. |
| `SC-A-5` | deferred | `KO-3` — A7: a profile whose role flags contradict a declared role is refused, naming both. The flags are `hook-framework` §8's and `EX-5`'s compatibility check is what reads them; the row asserts the operator refusing on their verdict, which is `KO-3`'s. |
| `SC-A-6` | deferred | `KO-3` — A8: a profile absent from the operator's catalog is refused, naming the profile and the catalog. The catalog is a property of the running operator — there is no such object today, so there is nothing for the row to name. |
| `SC-A-7` | deferred | `KO-3` — A9: a key that is not one of `cluster-config` §4 R1's six role names is refused, listing all six. The six are already normative and already enforced by the loader; the row is about the webhook echoing the closed set back, which needs the webhook. |
| `SC-A-8` | deferred | `KO-3` — A3/K6: a second `SipxCluster` in a namespace that already holds one is refused, naming the existing resource. Singleton-per-namespace is a statement about API-server state, so the row needs a real API server — `KO-3`'s Acceptance already requires envtest-class or k3s tests, which is where this lands. |
| `SC-A-9` | deferred | `KO-3` — A2: a rejected *update* against a resource already reconciling leaves `status` and every managed object untouched, and the last accepted generation keeps running. Needs both halves at once — a webhook to reject and a running reconcile loop to observe as undisturbed — so it is the last of the `SC-A` rows to become testable, not the first. |

## SipxCluster — observed status (§10)

| Row | Status | Proved by / deferred to |
|---|---|---|
| `SC-S-1` | deferred | `KO-3` — S1/S3: freshly accepted, no pod ready — `Ready: False`, and every role's ready count is the observed one rather than the declared one. The distinction is the entire `SC-S` family's premise and it only exists once something observes a fleet. |
| `SC-S-2` | deferred | `KO-3` — S3/S8: every role at its declared count and the last probe `Pass` — `Ready: True` carrying the run id. Needs the reconcile loop and a probe result to read; `ET-4`'s control API supplies the latter and `KO-3` is what reads it into `status`. |
| `SC-S-3` | deferred | `KO-3` — S4: a pod that reports nothing within the operator's interval drives its condition to `Unknown` naming the node — never to `True` by omission. The interval is the operator's, so the row cannot be stated against anything else. |
| `SC-S-4` | deferred | `KO-3` — S5: with a shard still draining, `ShardMapConverged: False` names the shard, `observedShardMap` stays at `n`, and `observedGeneration` stays behind `metadata.generation`. `observedGeneration` is an API-machinery fact; the drain is `KO-4`'s sequencing, and this row's verdict is `KO-3`'s status reconciliation reporting it. |
| `SC-S-5` | deferred | `KO-3` — S6: a key added with `mint: false` and not yet held everywhere gives `KeysDistributed: False` naming the key id and the lagging nodes, flipping `True` only when every verifier holds it. The `mint: false`-first ordering is `affinity-token` §6 K1 and is proved there; what defers is the operator observing which nodes have caught up. |
| `SC-S-6` | deferred | `KO-3` — S8: a `Fail { step: Invite }` probe surfaces as the verdict with its step and `Ready: False`, and the operator does nothing else — no rollback, no restart, no scale change. Half the row is an assertion about actions *not* taken, which needs a loop that could have taken them. |
| `SC-S-7` | deferred | `KO-3` — S7: a node refusing a profile that admission accepted gives `ProfileCompatible: False` naming the node and the refusing rule. This is the image-skew case — admission judged the operator's catalog, the node judged its own build, and nothing else in the system surfaces the gap. Needs a fleet whose nodes can disagree with the operator, so it is an envtest/k3s row. |
